question: Malignant mesothelioma typically develops within 5 years of initial asbestos exposure, making it straightforward to establish occupational causation in compensation claims.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Mesothelioma has a latency of 20–50 years — one of the longest of any occupational cancer. This creates severe medicolegal challenges: the patient may not remember the exposure, the employer may be dissolved, and medical records from decades ago may be unavailable.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Mesothelioma has a latency period of 20–50 years from initial exposure. This extreme latency makes causation extremely difficult to establish and often means the employer or exposure site no longer exists when the disease manifests.
